questions.prompt: Give the two conditions for Coulomb blockade in a metallic dot.
questions.solution: (i) The charging energy must exceed the thermal energy, $E_C=e^2/2C\gg k_BT$ (Eqs. 10.7, 10.13; Fig. 10.2 shows the oscillations washing out as $k_BT/E_C$ grows). (ii) The tunnel coupling must be weak, so that the charge on the dot is well defined: the dwell time on the dot is the longest time scale (Sec. 10.2), equivalent to a tunnel resistance $R_T\gg h/e^2$.
questions.checkerNote: The book states the weak-tunneling condition in words (Sec. 10.2) and does not print R_T >> h/e^2; that form is the standard criterion, kept as an equivalence.

questions.prompt: Write the steady-state solution of the sequential-tunneling master equation for a chain of charge states.
questions.solution:
Detailed balance between neighbouring charge states (Eq. 10.25) gives
$$\Gamma_{N-1,N}\,P(N)=\Gamma_{N,N-1}\,P(N-1)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad P(N)=P(N-1)\,\frac{\Gamma_{N,N-1}}{\Gamma_{N-1,N}},$$
which determines all $P(N)$ up to a constant. Normalization $\sum_NP(N)=1$ fixes the constant.

questions.prompt: Eq. (10.56) gives $G=e^2\sum_\sigma\int\frac{d\xi}{2\pi}\frac{\Gamma_L\Gamma_R}{\Gamma_L+\Gamma_R}A(d\sigma,\xi)\left(-\frac{\partial n_F}{\partial\xi}\right)$ in units $\hbar=1$. Take the Lorentzian $A(d\sigma,\xi)=\Gamma/[(\xi-\xi_d)^2+(\Gamma/2)^2]$ with $\Gamma=\Gamma_L+\Gamma_R$ and find $G$ at $T=0$ for a symmetric non-interacting level on resonance, $\xi_d=0$ and $\Gamma_L=\Gamma_R$.
questions.solution:
At $T=0$, $-\partial n_F/\partial\xi=\delta(\xi)$, so each spin gives
$$G_\sigma=e^2\,\frac{1}{2\pi}\,\frac{\Gamma_L\Gamma_R}{\Gamma_L+\Gamma_R}\,A(0)=\frac{e^2}{2\pi}\cdot\frac{\Gamma}{4}\cdot\frac{4}{\Gamma}=\frac{e^2}{h}.$$
With two spins, $G=2e^2/h$.

questions.prompt: Ex. 10.2. A single-level dot (Eq. 10.8) is in sequential tunneling. (a) Write the master equations for $P(0), P(\uparrow), P(\downarrow), P(d)$ with rates $\Gamma_{\beta\alpha}$ for the transition $\alpha\to\beta$. (b) In the large-$U$ limit with a degenerate level, find $P(0)$ and $P(\sigma)$. (c) For a Zeeman-split level with only $P(0)$ and $P(\uparrow)$ occupied, find both occupations. (d) Find the current from Eq. (10.26) and the linear conductance.
questions.solution:
Book Exercise 10.2. (a) Steady state (Eq. 10.11) for the empty state: rate out equals rate in,
$$\big(\Gamma_{\uparrow0}+\Gamma_{\downarrow0}\big)P(0)=\Gamma_{0\uparrow}P(\uparrow)+\Gamma_{0\downarrow}P(\downarrow),$$
and similarly for $P(\uparrow),P(\downarrow),P(d)$, with $\Gamma_{\beta\alpha}=\Gamma^L_{\beta\alpha}+\Gamma^R_{\beta\alpha}$ and $\sum P=1$.
(b) With degenerate spins and $P(d)=0$ (large $U$), $P(0)=\dfrac{\Gamma_{01}}{\Gamma_{01}+2\Gamma_{10}}$ and $P(\uparrow)=P(\downarrow)=\dfrac{\Gamma_{10}}{\Gamma_{01}+2\Gamma_{10}}$, where $\Gamma_{01}$ is the removal rate and $\Gamma_{10}$ the addition rate.
(c) With the Zeeman split and only two states, $P(0)=\dfrac{\Gamma_{0\uparrow}}{\Gamma_{0\uparrow}+\Gamma_{\uparrow0}}$ and $P(\uparrow)=\dfrac{\Gamma_{\uparrow0}}{\Gamma_{0\uparrow}+\Gamma_{\uparrow0}}$.
(d) The rates are $\Gamma^x_{\uparrow0}=\Gamma_xn_F(\varepsilon-\mu_x)$ and $\Gamma^x_{0\uparrow}=\Gamma_x[1-n_F(\varepsilon-\mu_x)]$ for $x=L,R$. Eq. (10.26) then gives
$$I=e\,\frac{\Gamma_L\Gamma_R}{\Gamma_L+\Gamma_R}\big[n_F(\varepsilon-\mu_R)-n_F(\varepsilon-\mu_L)\big],\qquad G=\frac{e^2}{\hbar}\frac{\Gamma_L\Gamma_R}{\Gamma_L+\Gamma_R}\,\frac{1}{4k_BT\cosh^2[(\varepsilon-\mu)/2k_BT]},$$
a thermally broadened peak whose height grows as $1/k_BT$.
questions.checkerNote: Part (d) forms taken from the exercise statement (E.10.3)-(E.10.6); overall sign of I follows the book's convention.

questions.prompt: Ex. 10.6. Starting from Eqs. (10.56) and (10.69), show that in the weak-tunneling limit $\Gamma\ll k_BT$ the conductance reproduces the master-equation result of Ex. 10.2 for large $U$.
questions.solution:
Book Exercise 10.6. In the limit $\Gamma\ll k_BT$ the Lorentzians become delta functions,
$$A(d\sigma,\omega)\to 2\pi\big[(1-\langle n_{\bar\sigma}\rangle)\,\delta(\omega-\xi_d)+\langle n_{\bar\sigma}\rangle\,\delta(\omega-\xi_d-U)\big].$$
For large $U$ the second delta lies far above $\mu$ and drops out. Eq. (10.70) then gives $n=(1-n)\,n_F(\xi_d)$, so $n=n_F/(1+n_F)$ and $1-n=1/(1+n_F)$. Inserting into Eq. (10.56),
$$G=2e^2\frac{\Gamma_L\Gamma_R}{\Gamma_L+\Gamma_R}\,\frac{1}{1+n_F(\xi_d)}\left(-\frac{\partial n_F}{\partial\xi}\right)_{\xi_d},$$
a thermally broadened peak of height proportional to $\Gamma_L\Gamma_R/[(\Gamma_L+\Gamma_R)k_BT]$. This equals the master-equation result of Ex. 10.2 for a degenerate level with large $U$, where $P(0)+P(\sigma)=1/(1+n_F)$ is the probability that the spin-$\sigma$ level is available.

questions.prompt: Ex. 10.7. For $\varepsilon_{d\uparrow}=\varepsilon_{d\downarrow}=\varepsilon$, show that the self-consistent solution of Eq. (10.70) with the spectral function of Eq. (10.69) at $T=0$ is given in closed form. Use $\Gamma$ for the full width.
questions.solution:
Book Exercise 10.7. Define $F(E)=\int_{-\infty}^{0}\frac{d\omega}{2\pi}\frac{\Gamma}{(\omega-E)^2+\Gamma^2/4}=\tfrac12-\tfrac1\pi\arctan\frac{2E}{\Gamma}$. Eq. (10.70) with Eq. (10.69) gives, for $\langle n_\sigma\rangle=\langle n_{\bar\sigma}\rangle=n$,
$$n=(1-n)\,F(\varepsilon)+n\,F(\varepsilon+U)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad n=\frac{F(\varepsilon)}{1+F(\varepsilon)-F(\varepsilon+U)}.$$
Checks: $n\to1$ for $\varepsilon\ll-U$ (both $F\to1$), $n\to0$ for $\varepsilon\gg0$, and $n\approx\tfrac12$ between the resonances for $U\gg\Gamma$ ($F(\varepsilon)\approx1$, $F(\varepsilon+U)\approx0$). In the book's notation $n=n_0/(1-n_U+n_0)$ with $n_0=F(\varepsilon)$ and $n_U=F(\varepsilon+U)$.
